## Introduction 

In this notebook, we are reverse engineering the story, [CEOs gave heavily during legislative session, exposing loophole in NC's fundraising ban](https://www.wral.com/archive/17716104/)

## Load libraries

Loading required libraries for this analysis.

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
install.packages('refinr')
options(scipen=999)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(refinr)
library(janitor)
```

## Load and Cleaning Data

In this section, describe the source of the data, write a basic data dictionary for data you are working with, and discuss any caveats or issues you discovered working with this data. 

```{r}
donors_nc <- read_csv("data/donors_nc.csv")

cleaned_donors_nc <- donors_nc |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    city = str_to_title(city),
    profession = str_to_title(profession),
    street_line1 = str_to_title(street_line1),
    street_line2 = str_to_title(street_line2),
    employer_name = str_to_title(employer_name),
    zip = str_sub(zip, 1, 5),
    date = mdy(date),
    amount = parse_number(amount)
  )
cleaned_donors_nc
```

## Sentences to Engineer
In this notebook, we are reverse engineering five sentences from the story.
I cleaned the data column and output of the date, zip code, and city name. 
### Sentence 1

* **Sentence text**: 
R.H. Barringer's board chair, Jasie Barringer, donated another $8,200 in-session, and Teresa Craig kicked in another $5,200 to Berger. The North Carolina Beer & Wine Wholesalers Association PAC gave $18,400 during the week before session and on opening day."

* **Analysis summary**: [Write up two to three sentences describing the results of your analysis.  Were you able to confirm the finding? If not, why not?] 

We were able to confirm the finding by looking at the date. The first donation I found was the was Teresa's donation of 5,200 which was on 5/18/18, by sorting by the date we can find the donations leading up to that date. Low and behold, Teresa's was there as previously mentioned, Barringer donated 5,200 that date as well as three 1,000 donations after (combining to 8,200), and when you look at the donations in the week leading up to it by the association, it adds up to 18,400 perfectly. 


```{r}
sentence_one <- cleaned_donors_nc |>
  filter(name_clean == "TERESA S CRAIG" | name_clean == "JASIE S BARRINGER" | name_clean == "NC BEER & WINE WHOLESALERS ASSOC PAC")
sentence_one |>
  group_by(date)

```

### Sentence 2

* **Sentence text**: Scott Prestage, with Prestage Farms, gave Moore's campaign $5,200 right at the end of session, after the General Assembly passed legislation meant to make lawsuits against hog farms harder to win. Going back to the beginning of the year, people connected to Prestage Farms gave Moore $31,000 in campaign donations. Half are dated two-and-a-half months before the session began. The rest came in the session's closing days or the day after the session ended.

* **Analysis summary**: [Write up two to three sentences describing the results of your analysis.  Were you able to confirm the finding? If not, why not?]
Scott Prestage would end up donating $5,200 twice to Friends of Time Moore, on 3/1/18 and again on 6/28/18. People associated with Prestage Farms would donate around $31,000 to the Friends of Tim Moore. 


```{r}
sentence_two <- cleaned_donors_nc |>
  filter(name_clean == "TERESA S CRAIG" | name_clean == "JASIE S BARRINGER" | name_clean == "NC BEER & WINE WHOLESALERS ASSOC PAC")
sentence_one |>
  group_by(date)

```
